title: The box on the bottom
topic: At Port Houston's Barbours Cut and Bayport container terminals, Kaleris RTG Optimization software plans the order of yard crane moves to avoid blocked stacks, while ILA operators still run the cranes.
hook: Why is your box always at the bottom?

treatment.logline: At Port Houston the hard part of a crane move is picking which box comes next, and optimization software now plans that order while ILA operators still run the cranes.
treatment.cold_open: A smiling gantry crane straddles a stack as a truck rolls in underneath. The orange box the driver came for sits at the bottom, and before second three a third box thunks down on top of it and the crane's eyes go wide.
treatment.turn: Kaleris says up to 20 percent better crane productivity, and the film draws that number as a dashed ceiling the bar bumps its head on, a vendor figure and a ceiling, never an average, while the people in the cabs stay at the controls.
treatment.button: Same truck, same stack, and this time the orange box is already on top. One lift onto the chassis, the operator nods, and the truck rolls out of the gate. Same crane, same hands, a better next move.

hero.name: the rubber-tired gantry crane with a face
hero.why: it is the machine the story is about, a yellow gantry with a visor face on its girder and an operator in its cab, and no film has drawn it

states.state: buried at the bottom of a stack under other boxes, worried
dug out at last while the driver waits
set down last when the stack is planned, so it lands on top
on top, lifted in one move onto the truck and rolling out of the gate

scenes.vo: A truck rolls into Port Houston for one orange container. It sits at the bottom of a stack, buried under other boxes.

draw.subject: the driver
draw.action: rolls in under the crane holding an orange slip up at the windshield
draw.emotion: the crane looks down at it, happy

draw.subject: a blue box
draw.action: drops onto the stack with a squash, right on top of the orange box at the bottom
draw.emotion: the orange box flinches and the crane's eyes go wide

draw.subject: the boxes above the orange one
draw.action: ring red one after another
draw.emotion: the orange box's eyes peek up, worried

scenes.vo: So the crane has to dig, lifting box after box to reach it, while the driver waits below.

draw.subject: the crane
draw.action: hoists the top box off the stack and swings it aside
draw.emotion: the operator in the cab grits their teeth

draw.subject: the second and third boxes
draw.action: come off one after another as a tally fills, then the orange box finally swings up

draw.subject: the driver
draw.action: drums their fingers on the wheel and checks the clock

scenes.vo: Port Houston was managing 142 of these rubber-tired gantry cranes at its Barbours Cut and Bayport terminals, on the Houston Ship Channel.

draw.subject: a container ship
draw.action: glides up the channel past the quay cranes

draw.subject: rows of gantry cranes
draw.action: pop up across the yard one after another as the counter climbs to 142

draw.subject: two map pins
draw.action: drop on the two terminals along the channel

scenes.vo: Those terminals see up to 12,000 truck visits a day, and a driver picking up comes for one particular box.

draw.subject: a line of trucks
draw.action: stretches back from the gate as headlights stream in and the counter runs to 12,000

draw.subject: the drivers in line
draw.action: hold up slips, each with a different coloured box on it
draw.emotion: the front driver grins and waves an orange slip

scenes.vo: The pressure keeps building. 2025 was a record year for containers at Port Houston, and volumes are forecast to keep growing.

draw.subject: the yard stacks
draw.action: rise a tier past the crane's visor as a ship noses in behind

draw.subject: the counter
draw.action: runs up to 4,303,345 as containers stream off the ship, twenty-foot units

draw.subject: the yard stacks
draw.action: grow a tier taller behind the ship

scenes.vo: So which move should a crane make next? Software from a company called Kaleris now helps decide.

draw.subject: the operator in the cab
draw.action: scratches their head at a jumbled list of jobs

draw.subject: the cab screen
draw.action: lights up and the jobs snap into a neat column

scenes.vo: It is called RTG Optimization. It plans the order of crane moves to avoid blocked stacks, inside the terminal's own operating system.

draw.subject: a fan of job cards
draw.action: spreads out like a dealt hand in front of the operator

draw.subject: the job cards
draw.action: shuffle and land in order, numbered 1 to 5, the orange card rising to the top

draw.subject: the stack
draw.action: rewinds and rebuilds with the orange box set down last, so it lands on top, while its job card reads 1

scenes.vo: It sends cranes where the demand is, using better data on what the yard needs.

draw.subject: the crane markers on the yard map
draw.action: unbunch from one red block and spread across the yard

draw.subject: a dispatcher at the yard screen
draw.action: taps it and a green route draws from a crane to the orange box

scenes.vo: It didn't start everywhere at once. The rollout began with truck moves in one small section of the yard.

draw.subject: a dashed fence
draw.action: drops around one small corner of the yard while the rest stays grey

draw.subject: two trucks
draw.action: roll into the lit corner and one crane lights up inside it

scenes.vo: Lessons from those early stages became custom filters and workflow changes that improved the operators' experience.

draw.subject: the operator
draw.action: marks a job card on the screen with a finger
draw.emotion: the operator purses their lips, deciding

draw.subject: a funnel
draw.action: drops onto the list and the clutter falls away, leaving three clean cards

scenes.vo: People still run the cranes. Port Houston operations chief Ryan Mariacher says the system works in tandem with the skilled labor of the ILA, the International Longshoremen's Association.

draw.subject: two crane operators in hard hats
draw.action: stride to the crane's ladder and one climbs on
draw.emotion: the lead operator grins back at the other

draw.subject: the quote card
draw.action: slides up and the words IN TANDEM stamp onto it

draw.subject: a row of hard hats
draw.action: bobs up along the bottom of the card

scenes.vo: Kaleris reports up to a 20 percent gain in yard crane productivity. That is the company's own figure, and up to means a ceiling.

draw.subject: a productivity bar
draw.action: shoots up beside the crane

draw.subject: a stamp
draw.action: thumps VENDOR FIGURE onto the bar

draw.subject: the bar
draw.action: bonks its head on a dashed ceiling and wobbles

scenes.vo: So back to that truck. This time the orange box is already on top. Same crane, same hands, a better next move.

draw.subject: the orange box
draw.action: sits on top of the stack and bounces as the truck pulls in

draw.subject: the crane
draw.action: lifts the orange box in one move and sets it on the chassis

draw.subject: the truck
draw.action: rolls out through the gate with the orange box as the boom lifts
